inspiration: Two-layer lava surface: one atlas is sampled twice with two different scroll offsets and blended, so molten rock moves without flipbook frames (crates/openeq-render/src/shaders/lava.wgsl, line 15). Recreate with our own lava texture pair and our own scroll speeds.

Waterfall curtains: colour and opacity scroll independently from one diffuse texture, cut out at a low alpha threshold, drawn with alpha blend and depth test but no depth write (docs/EQG_WATERFALL_RENDERING.md). A model for falling sheets of water or magic curtains.

Detail tint layer: a second colour texture on its own UV scale is multiplied over the base terrain colour (docs/EQG_TER_LAYERED_COLOR.md). Recreate as a cheap per-biome grime or moss layer on our own UVs.
Fixture-only animation: a hanging lamp rotates on one axis while its mount stays fixed, on a short authored loop (docs/WLD_LAMP_ANIMATION.md). Useful for chandeliers, signs and hanging lanterns.

Spell effects anchor to hand sockets on the skeleton. In first person, where the body is not drawn, they use camera-relative hand positions (docs/SPELL_EFFECT_RENDERING.md). A clear rule for casting visuals in our own rigs.

Ambient light from a time-of-day colour table sampled at fixed ticks, with the sky's reserved colour column feeding environment light (docs/SKY_LIGHT_COLOR_INPUTS.md). Recreate as our own day-cycle ramp per zone.
Per-zone fog and clip data kept in a flat table with separate fog sets per time band (crates/openeq-assets/data/peq-zone-environment.txt, header). A good data layout for zone mood in our own content.

XML-defined UI: buttons and gauges use state art (normal, pressed, hovered, disabled) and gauge fills are clipped to a fraction (crates/openeq-ui/README.md). Useful for our HUD bars and inventory frames.

briefs.label: Molten pool
briefs.why: A glowing surface that reads as hot from far away; the motion comes from two slow scrolls, not frame animation.
briefs.keep: two offset layers; bright seams; scroll speeds that differ
briefs.change: a cracked crust in our own pattern; a cooler violet tint; rim glow only on the edge
briefs.fit: silhouette at 375 wide: yes (a flat pool with a bright rim); signature behaviour: two-layer scroll; signature sound: none in donor; resemblance target 20-30 percent. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.

briefs.label: Falling sheet
briefs.why: A waterfall reads as moving from one textured curtain with alpha scrolling, so it is cheap and still reads well at distance.
briefs.keep: independent colour and opacity scroll; alpha cutoff; no depth write
briefs.change: our own sheet shape (wider at the top, frayed bottom); a foam strip at the base; a different noise pattern
briefs.fit: silhouette at 375 wide: yes (tall vertical band); signature behaviour: scroll; signature sound: none in donor. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.

briefs.label: Hanging lantern
briefs.why: A small moving light on a still mount gives a room life without a physics cost.
briefs.keep: one-axis rotation on the head only; fixed mount; short loop
briefs.change: swing on a chain instead of a spin; a warm ember colour; a brass cage ornament
briefs.fit: silhouette at 375 wide: small, weak; signature behaviour: swing; signature sound: none in donor. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.

briefs.label: Casting hand glow
briefs.why: Spell visuals stick to the hands, and first person gets its own camera-relative anchor, so casting always reads.
briefs.keep: socket anchoring; camera-relative fallback for first person
briefs.change: our own socket names and rune shapes; a colour per school; a motion arc that curls up
briefs.fit: silhouette at 375 wide: hand-sized, weak; signature behaviour: anchored cast; signature sound: none in donor. Rule: recreate as a clearly distinct original, never a copy.
